_comment: The structural half of the judgment-pass contract. Prompt bodies live in
references/agent-prompts.md and nowhere else; this file holds only ids,
dispatch metadata, and locators. A `find` string is a locator, not a copy:
scripts/passes.py refuses to emit when it does not match exactly `count`
times, and tests/test_passes.py fails when one goes stale. A copied prompt
body would drift undetectably, which is why there are none here.
`tier` mirrors the model-tier table in references/portability.md. It is
duplicated here so a dispatcher does not have to parse prose, and
tests/test_passes.py parses that table and fails if the two disagree.
What the two band names in `tier` mean, for a dispatcher that has its
own tier vocabulary and has to map onto it. They are RELATIVE to what
the caller has enrolled - not model names, and not absolute vendor
tiers. Mapping `supervisor` onto a fixed top tier is wrong twice: it
ages out when a line-up changes, and it is already wrong on any
deployment whose strongest enrolled model sits below that tier, where
it asks for a model the caller cannot route to and fails at dispatch.
`supervisor` means the best the caller actually has, whatever that is.
A runtime with one model runs every pass on it. That is a supported
configuration, not a degraded one - see the head of the model-tier
section in references/portability.md.

supervisor.means: the strongest model the caller has available; never tiered down
supervisor.failure_mode: silent - a weak read here produces a report that looks complete and is not

mid.means: any capable model; equals the ceiling when the caller has only one
mid.failure_mode: visible - a weak read here produces a thinner report and the findings are simply absent

_comment: The reduce half of Step 3. A dispatcher that fans out the passes and
stops there has run half the design: the passes disagree on purpose,
and nothing downstream reads their files directly. Declared here so
the shape is discoverable rather than inferred from six writes with no
consumer.
merge.reads: the `writes` file of every dispatched pass
merge.produces: the arbitrated finding set that Step 4 writes to report.md
why_not_delegable: It is judgment over other agents' output, including E's veto over A's
deletions, graded against references/comment-evidence.md - which SKILL.md
requires the supervisor to have read itself rather than hand to an agent.
Delegating the merge means grading evidence against a filename.

why_not_derived: meta.json carries no <side>, and no base at all under worktree scope,
so rendering this line means inventing report format - which
references/report-format.md owns and this contract does not touch. The
orchestrator already renders it for every markdown file the round
writes; it passes the same string here.

why: Agent S's prompt carries a worked example. Extracted verbatim it
dispatches S against a feature nobody asked for, and S returns a
confident boundary for it - a scope drawn one file narrow leaves that
file reviewed by nobody, with nothing in the output to say so.
